question.problem: The lamina $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,-y\le x\le y\}$ has the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=6{x}^{2}.$ Find the moment of the lamina about the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{x}={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is represented as a type II plane region and $\lambda (x,y)=6{x}^{2}.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}y\cdot 6{x}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}6{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-y}^{y}6{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2y[{\int }_{-y}^{y}3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2y\cdot {[{x}^{3}]}_{x=-y}^{x=y}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2y\cdot 2{y}^{3}\text{ }\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4{y}^{4}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{4}{5}{y}^{5}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =\frac{4}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
